quotes.text: AI doesn't care that your virtual machines are in someone else's data center. It cares about your data structure, your security posture, and your governance model.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints why moving servers alone does not make an organization AI ready.

quotes.text: AI projects don't fail because models are bad. They fail because the data feeding them is inconsistent, inaccessible, and undocumented.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear thesis on the real root cause of failed AI projects.

quotes.text: Locking data down isn't governance. Governance is structured transparency, knowing who touched what when and whether they had the right to.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a crisp definition of governance that goes beyond restriction.

quotes.text: Migration is a logistics project. Architecture is a strategic act. If your cloud strategy still reads like a relocation plan, you've already lost a decade.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the episode's call to architect instead of merely migrating.

quotes.text: The success metric has changed from percentage of servers moved to percentage of decisions we can trace and defend.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Proposes a concrete new success metric for cloud programs.

chapters.title: Cloud first is not AI ready
Why lift and shift fails AI

takeaways: Lift and shift preserves old permissions, untagged data and silos, which makes a migrated estate cloud ready but AI hostile.
AI readiness rests on data structure, lineage and governance, mature MLOps and people who own data and AI risk.
Unify the data estate, enforce governance as code and automate monitoring so policies keep pace with AI workloads.
hook: Many organizations move their servers to Azure and assume they are ready for AI, only to find their data, permissions and governance cannot support it. This episode is for IT leaders and cloud architects planning or finishing a migration. It explains why lift and shift fails AI and lays out a three-step strategy to unify, fortify and automate your cloud.
